qualification.text: Reflow is an early-stage MIT Go core and local proxy for budget-bounded Responses continuation, decoupled from CPA. It preserves client-managed login, keeps discarded tool calls from clients, and tracks folded usage. Codex, Pi and external Magpie integrations share protocol regressions. A dev.5 preview is public. We have no verified adoption metrics; the proposed ecosystem value is reusable compatibility checks for tool round-trips, cancellation and history recovery.

api_credit_use.text: Credits would fund planned maintenance: small-batch, budget-capped API runs checking protocol compatibility, tool-use round-trips, and disconnect recovery. We would reproduce failures, compare upstream versions, review fixes, and validate releases. These proposed API workloads are separate from our previous ChatGPT subscription tests, which are not an API-spend baseline.

additional_context.text: A native ChatGPT-login Desktop session completed continuation, successful tool use, 18/18 and normal completion with protected files unchanged. Dot's file read produced no local Reflow inference requests. Earlier CLI samples retain a config-audit exception. Source CI passes on three OSes; native CI passes Ubuntu/macOS, with hosted Windows write failures. Linux arm64/Intel Mac are build-only. Magpie #4497 is a discussion. No quality gain or adoption claim.

facts_to_preserve: Synthetic upstream checks are not real-account acceptance
No verified adoption figures or quality-improvement claims
One prior real continuation occurred in a timed-out session
The later successful patched-client session triggered zero continuations

November 5 Desktop first completed two real turns without continuation. A subsequent single Desktop session completed one real continuation, matching retained-tool roundtrip, 18/18 and normal completion, with protected files unchanged. Both command exits were zero; the non-command patch return had no exit code, and its exact file effect was independently reconstructed. Dot separately returned a local-file marker with zero local Reflow inference requests. No all-platform, all-dot-feature or quality benefit claim is made.
Magpie patches are published in Reflow but are not a submitted or merged Magpie PR; issue #4497 is a design discussion
The official 0.165.0 session passed 9/9 and ended normally with zero continuations, after one command failure

One separately authorized official API session completed two streaming requests and a fixed local function roundtrip, with zero reasoning tokens and zero continuations; native-login totals remain separate.

The CLI total remains 26 sessions, 134 observed requests and four continuations; its historical config-audit exception is unchanged. Desktop is separate: three sessions, 18 observed requests including four failed stream requests, and one continuation. The latest Desktop sample has a clean within-trial protected-file audit; it does not repair historical CLI records.
The dev.5 prerelease is public with ten platform ZIPs and two verification files; all twelve unauthenticated asset downloads matched the frozen hashes.
Three platforms have binaries identical to the cited pre-tag native CI; Linux arm64 and Intel Mac packages have only cross-compilation and package checks.

November 4 source CI passes on all three platforms. Native Ubuntu and macOS pass all phases; hosted Windows retains the old write failures. The unmodified-workflow Ubuntu pass has no established cause, and historical failed runs remain unchanged.
Repository metadata is not adoption data; the publication verification downloads are not external usage.
Pi was accepted under the user-selected simulation scope and is not waiting on a real-login test.
No application fields were entered on the website and no support or maintainer-role option was selected.
